items.howItWorks: Relieves secondarily infected allergic/inflammatory skin conditions
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for secondarily infected allergic or inflammatory skin diseases such as eczema, contact dermatitis, seborrheic dermatitis, atopic dermatitis, photodermatitis, lichen simplex chronicus, intertrigo, exfoliative dermatitis, itching, psoriasis, and for first-degree burns.
items.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area 1 to 3 times a day.
items.precaution:
Do not use this medicine in patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or its components, to aminoglycoside antibiotics such as streptomycin, kanamycin, gentamicin, neomycin, or to bacitracin, or with a history thereof; skin infections (tuberculosis, syphilis, candidiasis, tinea, herpes zoster, herpes simplex, chickenpox, vaccinia, scabies, pubic lice, etc.); eczematous otitis externa with tympanic membrane perforation; ulcers (excluding Behcet's disease); second-degree deep (not exposed) or more severe burns and frostbite; perioral dermatitis; acne vulgaris; or rosacea.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant or possibly pregnant, breastfeeding, an infant or child, or have a history of hypersensitivity or allergic reaction to propylene glycol.

Strictly observe the prescribed dosage and administration.

When used in children, use under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Do not use for ophthalmic purposes.

Do not use for purposes other than treatment, such as after makeup or shaving.

Do not use the occlusive dressing method without a doctor's supervision.
items.adverse: If contagious impetigo, folliculitis, viral infection, boils, skin irritation, stinging pain, fever, burning sensation, itching, rash, redness, flushing, dry skin, pustular dermatitis, heat rash, worsening of wounds, pressure sores, pustulosis, hypersensitivity, skin discoloration, hypertrichosis, acneiform eruption, hypopigmentation, perioral dermatitis, allergic contact dermatitis, skin maceration, secondary infection, skin atrophy, striae, increased intraocular pressure when used on eyelid skin, glaucoma (blurred vision), edema, papules, small blisters, or the like occur, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

items.howItWorks: Treats gum inflammation and oral trauma needing hyaluronic acid
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for the treatment of inflammatory conditions such as gingivitis and gum bleeding, where the gingival mucosa requires an increased hyaluronic acid concentration, and for traumatic conditions such as after scaling, exfoliation, tooth extraction, or surgical procedures.
items.usage: Use continuously after brushing 3 to 4 times a day (after meals) for 3 to 4 weeks until all symptoms disappear. Apply this medicine to the gum tissue and gently massage with a finger so that it is well distributed over the mucosal surface.
items.precaution: Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are a patient with hypersensitivity reactions to this medicine or a child under 12 years of age. If symptoms persist or worsen, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

items.howItWorks: Treats athlete's foot and ringworm infections
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for athlete's foot, tinea cruris (jock itch), and tinea corporis.
items.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area (diseased area) once a day.
items.precaution: Do not use this medicine on the eyes or around the eyes, mucous membranes (oral cavity, nasal cavity, vagina), the genital area, the external genitalia, or affected areas (diseased areas) with severe eczema, moisture (dampness), erosion (maceration), fissures (cracking), or trauma (wounds). Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are an infant or young child, have a history of allergic symptoms (rash, redness, itching, dermatitis due to lacquer, etc.) to medicines or cosmetics, have an allergic constitution, or the affected area (diseased area) is on the face, suppurative (festering), or extensive. Strictly observe the prescribed dosage and administration. When used in children, use under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Use this medicine for external use only and do not use it internally. be careful not to let it get into the eyes, and if it does get into the eyes, rinse immediately with water. Do not use immediately if the affected area (diseased area) or its surroundings are dirty. Do not touch the eyes or mucous membranes with hands that have this medicine on them.
items.adverse: If rash, redness (congested reddening), itching, dermatitis due to lacquer and the like, edema (swelling), irritation, scaling, erosion (maceration), dryness, a tight feeling, blisters, or the like occur, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
items.interaction: When used together with warfarin, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

items.howItWorks: Relieves pain and inflammation from sprains and muscle aches
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for the analgesic and anti-inflammatory (anti-inflammation) treatment of sprains, bruises, muscle pain, joint pain, fracture pain, low back (waist) pain, stiff shoulders, neuralgia, and rheumatic pain.
items.usage: Attach to the affected area (diseased area) 1 to 2 times a day.
items.precaution:
Do not use this medicine on infants under 30 months of age, or on eczema, dermatitis due to lacquer and the like, or wound areas.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are a patient who has had allergic symptoms due to medicines or cosmetics, a patient with an allergic constitution, a patient with severe moisture (dampness) or erosion (maceration), a child, or pregnant or possibly pregnant or breastfeeding.

Strictly observe the prescribed dosage and administration.

When used in children, use under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Use this medicine for external use only.

If no improvement of symptoms is seen even after 5 to 6 days of use, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
items.adverse: If rash/redness (congested reddening), itching, or the like occur, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
